Subject: Weekly capacity ops: aligning sales pipeline, finance commits, and infra runway

Hi team —

Kicking off this week’s capacity ops thread. Goal: reconcile the next 10 weeks of pipeline movement against the GPU commitment calendar so we can make a call on the two near-term deals (ACME pilot + Orion POC) that have non-trivial A100-equivalent footprint. My ask for today:

- Sales (Karthik, Marissa): provide per-deal expected start week, committed slot count if signed, and expected signature date (or PO ETA).
- Finance (Laura): share timing constraints for PO processing and any approval windows that would impact when we must provision reserved slots.
- Infra (Ben): quick assessment of packing efficiency + fragmentation risk if we commit 16 A100-equivalent slots for the two deals during Oct–Dec.

Attached: Q3-deal-heatmap.xlsx (high level). Also adding HubSpot link for D-12894 for reference: https://hubspot.app/record/D-12894

What I want at end of day: a short table (per-deal) with week-of-start, requested slots, and an indication of whether Sales has a signed commitment or only a verbal. If we can get that we can decide whether to convert burst capacity to reserved for the quarter.

Thanks —
Stephanie

Stephanie —

Quick update on pipeline commitments. I’ve attached a CSV (forecast_by_deal.csv) with the per-deal weekly slot estimate. TL;DR for the two prioritized deals:

1) ACME Analytics (D-12894) — pilot
   - expected start week: 2027-10-04
   - conservative requested slots: 10 A100-equivalent
   - optimistic slots (if we enable heavier quantization): 7
   - signature status: sales has verbal, legal review in-progress (target signature 2027-09-28)

2) Orion POC — (Procurement contact copied)
   - expected start week: 2027-10-18
   - requested slots: 8 A100-equivalent (short bursty windows initially)
   - signature status: procurement working on PO (procurement@orion.ai), target 2027-10-01

Conservative combined request for Oct–Dec = 18 slots. I put an explicit worst-case column in the CSV assuming 80% conversion across adjacent deals giving peak-week demand of ~22 slots.

Inline note: the ACME ask includes a 6-week ramp where they need sustained low-latency at 75% of the peak request; that's what drives the slot count early.

Karthik

Subject: Re: Weekly capacity ops: aligning sales pipeline, finance commits, and infra runway

Thanks — good data. A few infra points and a conservative recommendation:

- Packing efficiency: for mixed short/long sequences we’re seeing ~1.15x inefficiency vs ideal for A100-equivalent pools. That pushes required physical slots up ~15% vs the raw requested slot counts.
- Fragmentation risk: committing 18 slots as a single reservation is fine if we can place them in a contiguous pool. If the topology forces two fragmented pools (e.g., 10 + 8 on different host classes) we’ll lose another ~10% efficiency.
- Burst vs reserved: if Sales can guarantee signed commitments by 2027-09-28 (ACME) and 2027-10-01 (Orion), I recommend converting the conservative 18-slot plan to reserved capacity for Oct–Dec and reserving an additional 6 burst slots for unexpected peak. That means reserve 18, keep 6 burst credits. If legal/finance timing slips, we keep all on burst and re-evaluate mid-September.

Drive note: infra packing analysis + placement constraints are in this doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cDriveLink (infra_notes.md attached).

Operational ask:
- If Sales is confident on the signature/PO dates, I need the exact PO lead time (Laura) so we can start procurement for reserved capacity by 2027-09-10 to meet the 10/01 start.

Ben
Head of Fleet Ops
Redwood Inference

- Infra (Ben) — provision capacity plan: prepare an invoice-ready reserved capacity request for 18 slots + 6 burst credits (contingent on signatures). Include placement constraints and expected efficiency delta (owner: Ben; due: 2027-09-10).
- Ops (Stephanie) — publish a short runbook for switching burst -> reserved and reversal steps if utilization diverges. (owner: Stephanie; due: 2027-09-12)

Attachments: capacity_commit_request.pdf (a short template Finance can use to attach to the vendor request). I’ll also open a brief Jira (OPS-4721) to track the procurement milestones.

If there are no objections I’ll mark the plan as tentative and begin coordinating with vendor procurement on 2027-08-25.

Marissa
